messages.subject: heatmap creation with non-numerical values
parts:
Dear all,

I am doing my PhD in social sciences. I wanted to construct a heatmap
from 2-columned nominal dataset for my data analysis. However, when i
try to reproduce the following code from the referenced website:
http://learnr.wordpress.com/2010/01/26/ggplot2-quick-heatmap-plotting/#more-2380,
i am receiving constanly error messages like Error in colMeans(x,
na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric.

Is it possible to handle my task via ggplot2. If not, what do you
recommend me? Since i do not have a programming background, i
appreciate your helps.

regards
sophie

messages.author: 2fbcafbd7f6caa85
messages.subject: Re: heatmap creation with non-numerical values
parts:
My guess is that the error comes from the gradient fill, which
requires a numeric. Use the default colour scale, or a discrete one
like so:

set.seed(42)
df<-data.frame(
variable1=head(LETTERS,5),
variable2=tail(LETTERS,5),
value=sample(letters[1:3],5,replace=TRUE)
)

p<-ggplot(df)+geom_tile(aes(x=variable1,y=variable2,fill=value))+scale_fill_brewer(palette='Set1',type='qual')
print(p)

Hope that helps,
Christophe

messages.subject: Re: heatmap creation with non-numerical values
parts:
Sorry, posted too fast. Here is a example with a fuller matrix and a
similar colour scheme as in your example:
set.seed(42)
df<-expand.grid(
variable1=head(LETTERS,5),
variable2=tail(LETTERS,7))
df$value<-sample(letters[1:5],nrow(df),replace=TRUE)

p<-ggplot(df)+geom_tile(aes(x=variable1,y=variable2,fill=value))+scale_fill_brewer(palette='Blues',type='seq')
print(p)

(See http://colorbrewer2.org/ for a good collection of palettes)

Christophe
